evidence.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.
On the surface of the earth, its value is 9.8 meters per square second or 32.2 feet per square second.
The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.
we would expect that the weight of an object would decrease with altitude.

objectives: Define weight as the gravitational force on a mass
Relate mass, gravitational acceleration, and weight with W = m*g
Explain universal gravitation and gravitational acceleration
Calculate how weight decreases with altitude
analysis.unsupportedReason: The source teaches the weight equation W = m*g, universal gravitation, and altitude-related weight change, which matches none of the listed activity equations.
